rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It shares the child's distinctive three-recital structure: identification of an international trade exhibition with dates and commercial purposes; citation of a joint resolution authorizing the President to invite States and foreign countries; and an explanation of the benefits of their participation. Both then use nearly identical operative language inviting the same classes of participants to the named event at the specified place and dates. C10 is a related and plausible antecedent for the general trade-fair invitation machinery, but its structure and wording are less closely aligned. C25 concerns international trade participation but lacks the same detailed sequence and close verbal correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the United States World Trade Fair is to be held at New York, New York, from April 14 to April 27, 1957, inclusive, for the purposes of exhibition, promotion, and sale of foreign products and services to the American trade and to the public
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas the First International Instrument Congress and Exposition is to be held at Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, from September 13 to 25, 1954, inclusive, for the purpose of exhibiting various kinds of scientific instruments and devices and the promotion of foreign and domestic trade and commerce in such products
shared_material.explanation: The opening recitals follow the same event-location-dates-purpose formula, adapted to a different exhibition.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the Congress, by a joint resolution approved July 27, 1956, has authorized the President of the United States of America, by proclamation or in such other manner as he may deem proper, to invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 28, 1954, authorized the President of the United States of America, by proclamation or in such other manner as he may deem proper, to invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, nearly verbatim authorization language occupying the same position in both proclamations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the participation by the States of the Union and foreign countries in the United States World Trade Fair will promote foreign and domestic commerce and will serve as a means of fostering good will among nations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas the participation by the States of the Union and foreign countries in the First International Instrument Congress and Exposition will advance the arts and sciences ... and further foreign and domestic commerce in these articles
shared_material.explanation: Both use a third recital explaining the substantive benefits expected from participation by States and foreign countries.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate in the United States World Trade Fair to be held in the Coliseum in New York, New York, from April 14 to April 27, 1957, inclusive
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby invite the States of the Union and all countries of the free world to participate in the First International Instrument Congress to be held at Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, from September 13 to September 25, 1954, inclusive
shared_material.explanation: The operative provisions have the same invitation, participant classes, event, location, and date sequence, with factual particulars substituted.
